_about.method: Read by eye from the photos and the City of Bern Orthofoto 2026 (flown March/April 2026, 10 cm). Hex colours are median pixel values of a hand-placed box in the named photo (sRGB, no colour calibration); 'light' says how neutral the light was. Positions: estimated on the orthophoto, accuracy ~2-5 m.
_about.confidence_scale: high = clearly visible in a recent photo; medium = visible but old photo (<=2018) or partly hidden; low = inferred from aerial or a single blurry view; needs an on-site photo
_about.trees_source: City of Bern tree register (baumkataster_station.geojson from the geometry agent, Letzte_Aenderung up to 2026-05-28) for species and planting year; photos for shape and season
_about.season_note: Late November: horse chestnuts bare or with last brown leaves; low sun from the south-south-west at midday (about 20 deg elevation) - long shadows across the square.

top_candidate.stretch: Hirschengraben north head (candidates.md choice): tram stop Hirschengraben platform B (7.437785, 46.946896) past the Bubenberg monument to platform C (7.438195, 46.946983), 38 m heading ENE; facts below also cover the promenade ~40 m south of the monument

status_nov_2026.summary: Not yet rebuilt. The city's ZBB plan (new underpass to Hirschengraben, monument to be moved to the middle of the square, 5 of 25 trees felled and replaced, bike parking removed) is approved by the canton (30 Oct 2025) but under appeal; start 'end of 2026 realistic' (Der Bund) / '2027/2028 depending on appeals' (bern.ch). The Mar/Apr 2026 orthophoto shows a row of site skips/containers and a long site cabin along the west edge of the square next to the tram track, and a food/market stand with parasols in the middle of the square.
status_nov_2026.confidence: medium (aerial is 7 months old; whether hoardings went up since is unknown - needs an on-site photo)

buildings.name: Hotel National, Hirschengraben 24 (corner Maulbeerstrasse; south end, outside the 40 m stretch but in view)

monument.what: Adrian von Bubenberg monument (Max Leu, 1897; restored 2015): bronze standing figure in armour on a tall stepped plinth of light reddish-grey granite with inscription 'ADRIAN VON BUBENBERG 1424-1479' in red letters, bronze helmet/weapon trophy and Bern bear shield on the plinth
monument.size: not measured - no reference of known size close enough; plinth with steps visibly about 3-4 times a person's height (rough estimate)
monument.plan: ZBB plan moves it to the middle of the square (not before construction)

trees.species: horse chestnut (Aesculus hippocastanum) x19 + double-flowered horse chestnut x2 in two rows; 3 Kobushi magnolias
trees.shape: heavily pollarded / box-pruned: short trunks (~3 m to the first knuckles, estimate) with knobbly 'fist' heads - very characteristic in winter
trees.season_nov: bare or nearly bare; summer crown dense, light green
trees.layout: two rows along the long axis of the square, ~6-8 m spacing (aerial estimate)

benches.what: a few benches along the east tree row and next to the monument; aerial shows dark-green rectangles ~2-2.5 m long and one larger brown wooden element ~3.5 m (estimates from the 10 cm aerial)
benches.type: unknown from available imagery - likely the standard dark-green Bern park bench (wood slats, cast-iron frame, with backrest) - NOT confirmed

bike_parking.what: long rows of bike stands along the east kerb and around the monument; ZBB plan removes the Hirschengraben bike parking

lamps_and_wires.what: tall grey steel tram poles (ring-banded, on a concrete foot) carrying the tram/trolleybus catenary and transverse span-wires; street lighting appears to be hung from span-wires (catenary lights) rather than on own poles - typical for Bern, not clearly visible in the available photos
lamps_and_wires.confidence: medium for poles/wires, low for lamp type

tram.what: tram tracks along the west side of the square, curving into Bubenbergplatz at the north end; tram stop 'Hirschengraben' (lines 3/6/7/8 area, red Bernmobil vehicles); 2 small transport buildings in OSM at Hirschengraben 2a/2b (shelters/kiosk)

signs.what: red-brown Swiss cycle-route signposts (Thun/Belp, Biel/Aarberg, Neuchatel/Kerzers, Konolfingen) on a tram pole at the north tip; no-entry sign 'ausgenommen Velo'; yellow bike symbols painted on the asphalt

fountain_south.what: J. V. Widmann fountain: round open temple (6 stone columns, copper-green ribbed dome with gilt crown) with bronze youth figure, at the south end (Hirschengraben/Bundesgasse) - landmark at the end of the view
